items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Dickie Wells and I would hang out together.

ctx.x: . . . and had really [admired], in the Basie band.

Oh yeah. Unfortunately my hero wasn’t there. Lester Young wasn’t there. He had some monsters in Lester’s place in the person of Don Byas, a killer, killer saxophone player, and Illinois Jacquet. They all came along after Lester. He still had some of the holdovers, like Sweets was still there – Harry "Sweets" Edison, that is. I first met Joe Newman in Basie’s band. Dickie Wells was still there. I held Dickie Wells in very high esteem. Dickie Wells was a unique trombonist in that less is more. Simple is good. His…
